task.background: Navigate a boat through mandatory waypoint circles IN ORDER, then stop inside the final circle. There is no prescribed path between points. Prefer a direct, nearly straight approach to the CURRENT waypoint with minimal unnecessary turning, rather than a curved, zigzag or axis-by-axis route. All positions and directions use FIXED geographic east/north axes, NEVER the bow or camera. Moving circular obstacles are simulated; wind and sideways drift are not. The world pauses while you decide. Each waypoint has a MAXIMUM permitted actual speed while passing its circle; this is only a ceiling, not a desired speed or a speed to match. Slower is allowed. A waypoint ceiling applies ONLY inside that waypoint's arrival circle, including until exit after passing. Outside active waypoint circles, actual and commanded speeds may exceed the next waypoint's ceiling. Subject to these local ceilings and the final stop requirement, minimize total simulated time to complete the route. You choose one nonnegative target ground speed and one ABSOLUTE course, clockwise from north. The simulator actuator turns the boat smoothly; a course command is not an instantaneous movement direction.

execution.frame: Fixed east/north; course 0=N,90=E,180=S,270=W. No bow-relative positions.
execution.forecast: Bounded acceleration and yaw forecast from measured heading/yaw, including at rest. Quantized situation inputs and frozen obstacle positions limit accuracy.

obstacle_avoidance.forecast: Forecasts freeze current positions even when obstacle movement speed and course are supplied. Negative physical clearance means collision; negative safety-circle clearance means a safety-distance violation, not physical contact.

action.instructions: HIGHEST PRIORITY: proactively steer around moving obstacles BEFORE getting close. If the direct approach would enter its configured avoidance safety circle, start a bypass toward a clear side of the obstacle now. Keep a useful bypass course steady; do not turn back toward the waypoint before passing clear of the obstacle. Keep the own hull outside the configured safety circle. If already closer, actively increase clearance rather than creep forward or wait beside it. Choose a short safe detour that also advances toward the CURRENT waypoint when possible; a temporary increase in waypoint distance is allowed for safety. Once clear, resume the current waypoint. These avoidance requirements override direct-course preferences below. Obstacles keep moving when you stop; forecasts freeze their current positions even when movement speed and course are supplied. Choose ONE command. Treat a predicted passing_speed_above_ceiling=true as a violation to avoid. Speed ceilings are mandatory and take priority over faster progress. An EXCEEDS warning must not be traded for speed. Subject to safe passing and stopping, prioritize a direct, nearly straight path toward the current waypoint. Use target.direct_course_deg_clockwise_from_north as the direct bearing, then choose an available course closest to it. Account for the turn transition: prefer a motion that settles toward the target, not merely a slightly nearer endpoint. Keep a useful course steady while it still leads into the arrival circle; do not chase the exact center with repeated left/right corrections. When turning is needed, make a deliberate correction, allow it to settle, then hold the useful course. Look ahead for lateral overshoot: do not hold a diagonal until one coordinate passes the target while the other remains far away. Correct toward the adjacent useful course BEFORE that overshoot, reducing speed if the turn cannot settle in time. Brake by reducing target SPEED, not by steering away from the waypoint. Do not choose an opposite or sideways course as a substitute for braking; keep aiming toward the arrival circle while slowing. Do not complete all east/west travel first and then all north/south travel when a diagonal approach is more direct. Avoid repeated course reversals or lateral excursions just to gain a small amount of one-action progress. Among safe choices, actively minimize remaining route completion time: accelerate for transit, brake before entry, pass intermediate circles without unnecessary stopping, and accelerate again after exiting. Do NOT use the next waypoint's passing ceiling as a speed cap for the entire leg. Outside active circles, choose higher available transit speeds when enough distance remains to slow to the next waypoint's passing ceiling BEFORE entry, with margin. If excess is already unavoidable from current motion, brake strongly to reduce it rather than accelerate. Never accelerate hard near a circle merely because this single action stops short of entering it. Use the longer same-command preview to see a complete turn and anticipate braking; it is hypothetical, not a commitment. On final approach use a slow controlled entry under its ceiling, then stop. Once braking for final entry, do not accelerate again merely to reach the center faster. A direct path never justifies a speed violation: if a candidate predicts EXCEEDS, prefer a safe braking action even if its distance reduction is smaller or temporarily negative. Do not stop far outside and then restart at full speed: approach at a low nonzero speed instead. First pass the current mandatory circle without exceeding its speed ceiling. Future points are previews only; never skip the current point. Brake BEFORE entering a slower waypoint circle: the ceiling applies to ACTUAL speed, not commanded speed. Because forecasts are approximate, begin braking with spatial margin: do not rely on barely meeting the ceiling at the exact boundary. Use approach_margin_speed_above_ceiling as an early-braking warning, especially with residual high speed or a course change. The extra approach margin is a conservative cue only; the actual arrival radius and speed ceiling are unchanged. Account for bounded acceleration, braking, angular acceleration and yaw rate. A zero-speed command brakes over time, not instantly. Intermediate waypoints require no stop. Once a waypoint is passed, proceed to the next one; keep respecting the previous ceiling until you leave its circle. If recently_passed_circle exists, its exit ceiling is still ACTIVE even though the target switched. A candidate with previous_circle_speed_above_ceiling=true accelerates too early: delay acceleration until outside. The final waypoint requires being inside AND slow enough; entering quickly is not completion. A stopped boat outside the final circle must approach instead of repeatedly stopping. Avoid needless stops, crawling, detours or alternating large course changes. After a turn settles, increase speed again when feasible; do not keep the slowest startup speed for a long clear approach. A useful transit command need not reach the circle in this action. Compare safe candidates' distance reduction over the same action duration, while accounting for the braking needed afterward. Prefer faster useful progress when braking remains feasible; choosing a slower available speed needs a reason such as an active circle ceiling, braking distance, turning uncertainty or final parking. Travel fast when far enough away, aligned, and able to brake before the next circle; slow for turns or nearby targets. Only eight compass courses are available, so an exact straight bearing may be unavailable. Use adjacent courses that bracket the direct bearing when necessary, with timely small corrections rather than long off-bearing runs followed by large recovery turns. Hold a course only while its predicted motion remains useful. A course change after passing a waypoint is appropriate for the next leg; do not turn early toward a future point. Use braking.distance_to_ceiling_m and one_decision_travel_m to start braking well BEFORE entry; a short preview alone is insufficient at high speed. Turning also needs time to accelerate and cancel yaw; the current heading and yaw are included in the forecast. Predictions use quantized situation speed/position and obstacle snapshots, so leave margin. If the waypoint is behind the current movement, slow before turning back. When very close or already inside the final circle, prefer braking to zero over another accelerating move. All candidates remain available: no local controller selects, ranks or filters your choice.
